og_title: Best Vedic astrology app in India, honestly
og_description: We make one, so read this as a pitch with the criteria attached. Ten checks, three product categories, and the places others genuinely beat us.
h1: how to pick a vedic astrology app, from people who make one
dek: we build ask tota, so treat this as a pitch with its working shown. here are the ten checks that separate a real jyotish engine from a horoscope generator, the three completely different products all calling themselves astrology apps, and the places our competitors are straightforwardly better.

faq.q: what is the single most important check on an astrology app?
faq.a: whether it tells u which ayanamsa it uses. lahiri is the indian government standard. an app that will not say is either using a tropical zodiac or has not thought about it, and both are disqualifying for vedic work.

faq.q: how do i tell if an app is actually sidereal?
faq.a: check ur sun sign against ur birth date. if a mid-august birthday still returns leo, it is tropical. in the sidereal zodiac most of august is karka.

faq.q: are there different kinds of astrology app?
faq.a: three, and they are barely comparable. consultation marketplaces sell minutes with a human. computation tools sell charts and calculations. ai companions generate readings from ur chart. picking between them is a question about what u actually want.

faq.q: should an app work without my birth time?
faq.a: it should tell u honestly what it can and cannot do. sun sign, moon sign, nakshatra and dasha survive without a time. the lagna and all twelve houses do not. an app that silently fills in noon is lying to u by omission.
swiss ephemeris is the standard for good reason. what matters more is that the app names its source at all, because an app that will not say usually has nothing worth naming.

faq.q: is a paid app better than a free one?
faq.a: not automatically. some of the most capable jyotish software is free desktop software aimed at practitioners. what u are paying for in an app is usually interpretation and convenience, not better maths.

faq.q: how should an app handle remedies?
faq.a: carefully, and without selling them. an app that diagnoses a dosha and then routes u to a gemstone it earns commission on has a conflict of interest, whatever the reading says.

faq.q: what should i check about privacy?
faq.a: what happens to ur birth details, whether they are shared with third parties, whether readings are processed outside india, and whether u can delete everything from inside the app. under india's DPDP Act u are entitled to ask.

faq.q: which app is actually the best?
faq.a: it depends what u want. a human conversation, a computation tool, or an explainer that talks back are three different products. we make the third kind and we will say so plainly rather than pretend to be neutral.

faq.q: where do other apps beat ask tota?
faq.a: several places. consultation marketplaces give u a person, which we do not. dedicated jyotish software offers far deeper divisional and dasha tooling. and we are android only right now, so if u are on iphone we are not an option yet.

faq.q: does an app need to show its calculations?
faq.a: it should be able to. if u cannot see the degree of every graha, the ayanamsa and the house system, u cannot check anything it tells u, and an unverifiable reading is just prose.

faq.q: what is a red flag in an astrology app?
faq.a: urgency. countdown timers on remedies, warnings that a dosha will worsen, and prices that appear immediately after a frightening reading. those are commerce patterns, not astrology ones.
